steps.action: Cite three published tectonic models for the eastward continuation of the Qinling–Dabie–Sulu belt into Korea: Gyeonggi indentation, a Hongseong–Yangpyeong–Odesan suture, and a Hongseong–Imjingang Belt linking the Gyeonggi Massif to North China.
steps.quote: Several tectonic models for this extension have been proposed

steps.action: State the open problems: unclear stratigraphic relations between the Early Neoproterozoic supracrustals and the Paleoproterozoic basement, and their depositional setting. Set the aim of clarifying them in the Paju–Yangju–Dongducheon area.
steps.quote: The aim of this study was to clarify the geological significance of the Early Neoproterozoic metasedimentary succession

steps.action: Map the area and describe the lithologies, outcrop structures and petrography of the gneisses and metasediments (Figs. 2-4), defining an 'alternation unit' with large-scale isoclinal folds.
steps.quote: The quartzites range in thickness from 5 to 30 m

steps.action: Image zircons by SEM-CL and date 19 metasedimentary and 4 gneiss samples by LA–MC–ICPMS U–Pb at KBSI, following previously described procedures, with reduction in Iolite and Isoplot.
steps.quote: performed using a Nu Plasma II multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry

steps.action: Add five previously dated samples (SYQ-1, YCQ-1, YCQ-3, GYS-3, SYS-2) from the authors' earlier study to the data set.
steps.quote: we also used three previously reported quartzite samples

steps.action: Filter analyses at <3% discordance and estimate per-sample detrital age populations, youngest grains and Permo-Triassic overgrowth ages (ca. 259-221 Ma) for the west, central and east parts. Estimate gneiss upper-intercept ages of 1873-1863 Ma.
steps.quote: Age data with < 3 % discordance were used to avoid analytical bias

steps.action: Compare the new detrital ages with the earlier mapping of the area as a Paleoproterozoic gneiss complex, and assign the calc schists and calc-silicates to the Early Neoproterozoic succession.
steps.quote: The present detrital zircon U-Pb age results for calc schist and calc-silicate with layered quartzite

steps.action: Document an outcrop of pebble-bearing quartz mica schist resting on banded granite gneiss in the northeast of the area.
steps.quote: the unconformity boundary between Middle Paleoproterozoic basement gneiss and Early Neoproterozoic pebble-bearing quartz mica schist

steps.action: Keep the reading that the alternation reflects an unconformable stratigraphic relationship (Neoproterozoic cover on Paleoproterozoic basement) later isoclinally folded, while noting that the boundary remains controversial.
steps.quote: the alternation of Middle Paleoproterozoic and Early Neoproterozoic rocks is likely related to an unconformable stratigraphic relationship

steps.action: Compare the integrated detrital age spectra (Fig. 10) with the local basement ages to infer proximal Gyeonggi sources for western and central quartzites and schists, and distal sources for eastern samples and calc schists.
steps.quote: are thought to have been mostly supplied by the proximal Middle Paleoproterozoic Gyeonggi Massif

steps.action: Match the overgrowth ages with published Late Permian to Early Triassic metamorphism and collision tectonics in the central Korean Peninsula, explaining the isoclinal folding.
steps.quote: preserve many overgrowths caused by Late Permian to Early Triassic metamorphism

steps.action: Estimate the maximum depositional age from the youngest detrital grains (984-918 Ma, n = 3, ca. 952 Ma) and the young age range of 1142-1092 Ma.
steps.quote: may indicate the upper sedimentation age limit of these rocks

steps.action: Compare the detrital spectra with compiled published spectra and with a compilation of 967 intrusive-rock ages (Figs. 12-13). The successions considered are the western Gyeonggi Massif, the Sangwon Supergroup and the southeastern North China Craton.
steps.quote: These results are markedly similar to those of the Early Neoproterozoic metasedimentary rocks from the western Gyeonggi Massif

steps.action: Use the Cawood et al. (2012) framework, which relates detrital age distributions to tectonic setting, to read the spectra as extensional and trailing-edge basin types.
steps.quote: lying in extensional and trailing edge settings as suggested by Cawood et al. (2012)

steps.action: Compare the lithological assemblages with published depositional interpretations of the Sangwon Supergroup and western Gyeonggi successions (marine shelf, tidal flats, rift setting).
steps.quote: are considered to have formed in a marine setting, via shoreline progradation on the continental shelf

steps.action: Conclude that the successions were deposited at ca. 0.98-0.92 Ga in marginal shallow-marine to fluvial environments under extensional and trailing-edge settings, on a margin linking the Korean Peninsula and the SE North China Craton.
steps.quote: were deposited in marginal shallow marine to fluvial environments under extensional and trailing edge settings

end.claim: The Paju–Yangju–Dongducheon metasediments were deposited unconformably on 1873–1863 Ma Gyeonggi basement at ca. 0.98–0.92 Ga, in marginal shallow-marine to fluvial environments under extensional and trailing-edge settings. The margin linked the central Korean Peninsula with the southeastern North China Craton, and was later folded by Permo-Triassic collision.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the per-sample detrital zircon U–Pb age populations and youngest-grain ages, neither the Neoproterozoic assignment, the provenance split nor the North China correlation would exist.

gates.evidence: Sampling extends earlier work (Kim et al., 2019, 2020) that had already assigned parts of the unit to the Neoproterozoic. Adding calc schists tests whether they too are Neoproterozoic, which they could have failed (p. 14). No stated hypothesis directs the choice of the 19 samples, and the tectonic models are not given distinct predictions. The <3% discordance threshold is stated but not said to have been fixed before the data were seen (p. 8).

limits: 1. The XML text contains only figure captions, so body quotes come from the PDF. No peer-review file was supplied. 2. No V check is performed: no reference materials, reproducibility of standards, alternative discordance thresholds or independent dating method are reported in the main text. The analytical procedures are deferred to Kim et al. 2020, 2021, and the supplement was not supplied. 3. The three cited tectonic models are not assigned distinct predictions or excluded explicitly. The North China linkage is favoured by similarity of spectra (inference). 4. The maximum depositional age rests on three youngest grains. The abstract's 'ca. 0.92 Ga' and the conclusion's '0.98–0.92 Ga' are not reconciled. 5. The YCGGN-5 age is 1863.2 ± 2.5 Ma in the text (p. 14) but 1832.2 ± 2.5 Ma in Fig. 9b. 6. Fig. 15 is cited on p. 18 but does not appear in the paper. 7. Sub-claims and statuses: basement gneiss ages 1873–1863 Ma (estimate_with_resolution); Neoproterozoic age of the calc schists (estimate_with_resolution); unconformable contact (best_explanation, from one outcrop, with the boundary admitted to be controversial); Permo-Triassic overgrowths at ca. 259–221 Ma (estimate_with_resolution); provenance split, proximal versus distal (best_explanation).
